source.check: returned unopposed: no contest in any division of the district (Ulster Herald, 22 April 1933, p. 5); named as a member at the statutory (first) meeting of the new council, Tuesday 6 June 1933, on the Finance Committee and a representative on the Ulster Tourist Development Association (Mid-Ulster Mail, 10 June 1933, p. 5, page image read); the division and member agree with the Irish News nominations list of 19 April 1933, p. 6 (image read, council-audit, Nov 2026)

note: Triennial election of the Dungannon rural district councillors, 1933. 'There will be no contest in any of the district electoral divisions of Dungannon Rural Council' (Ulster Herald, 22 April 1933, p. 5); the nominations list is printed in the Irish News, 19 April 1933, p. 6 (one name for each division; read on the page image, council-audit, Nov 2026). Eleven of the nineteen divisions are recorded by the meeting method (7 Nov 2026): each member is the 1930 return for the division and sat at the new council's statutory meeting on Tuesday 6 June 1933 (Mid-Ulster Mail, 10 June 1933, p. 5). Not recorded: Altmore, Clonavaddy, Crossdernott, Donaghmore and Granville (the 1930 members are not named at the meeting); Minterburn (Mr. M. Busby, the member from 1936, sits, not the 1930 member); Castlecaulfield (Colonel Howard and Mr. M. D. Brown both sit, and a Mr. M. Brown was co-opted); and Anahoe (both Mr. T. D. Givans and Mr. T. J. Cuddy appear). No poll was held; Tyrone's polling day was Wednesday 31 May 1933. division inferred from the 4 June 1930 return (F. T. Roulston); the Mid-Ulster Mail, 10 June 1933, p. 5 names the member as returned, sitting at the new council's first meeting, where Mrs. Brown, Mr. M. Brown and Mr. William Moffatt were co-opted. Returned unopposed.
